newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco and Spain to team up on drugs, immigration.
newsitem.headline: Morocco and Spain to team up on drugs, immigration.

text.p: Morocco will prevent illegal African immigrants going to Spain and wants European Union help in eradicating cannabis crops, Moroccan Interior Minister Driss Basri said on Friday.
Basri told a joint news conference with his visiting Spanish counterpart Jaime Mayor Oreja that they would strengthen cooperation over drug trafficking and illegal immigration.
"Africans will be turned back in Morocco before getting to Spain. Then we will send them back to their own countries...it will show our government's goodwill," Basri said.
"We asked the European Union to help us convert the cultivation of cannabis but so far we have not been satisfied (with the EU response)," he added.
The Spanish minister said the main issues discussed were drugs, followed by illegal immigration and also technical help for Morocco's elections.
"We want technical help on elections because we want our elections to be acceptable in our country but also in Europe, to prove our institutions are democratic," Basri added.
The two ministers said they would launch a joint work team to exchange information and fight drugs before next February.

"With this accord, justice authorities and concerned squads will combine efforts...We'll be able to track down drug traffickers in the places they are hiding in and help each other in our two countries," Basri said.
